question: Where do you go in OpenToonz to define which scanner and driver type will be used for scanning?
options: File → Preferences → Scanner
Scan & Cleanup → Define Scanner…
Settings → Device Manager → Scanner
Cleanup → Scan Settings → Driver

question: Which menu command merges Toonz Vector levels and standard Raster levels into a single animation level?
options: Xsheet → Merge TLV Levels
Xsheet → Merge Levels
Cells → Merge Levels
Level → Merge Levels
evidence_quote: Toonz Vector levels and standard Raster levels can be easily merged into a single animation level generated by flattening them according to their stacking order, using the Xsheet → Merge Levels command.

question: After installing FFmpeg, where in OpenToonz do you specify the path to the FFmpeg folder?
options: File → Preferences…, in the Import/Export category
Render → Output Settings…, in the File Settings subsection
Windows Control Panel → System → Environment Variables
File → Open Recent, in the FFmpeg section

question: Where can you customize the interval of the horizontal markers that divide the Xsheet into sections?
options: In the Preferences… → Interface dialog section
In the Xsheet → Scene Settings… dialog, using the Marker Interval option
In the Preferences… → Xsheet dialog section, using the Column Icon option
In the Xsheet → Scene Settings… dialog, using the Start Frame option

question: In which dialog do you choose the 'Scan Level' type when defining an animation level to scan?
options: Level Settings window
New Level dialog
Project Default Folders dialog
Xsheet/Timeline cell editor
evidence_quote: In the New Level dialog choose Scan Level from the Type: option menu and define its settings, then click the OK button.

question: What happens to the drawings' numbering when you set the Increment value to 2 in the New Level dialog?
options: Drawings are numbered 1, 2, 3, etc.
Drawings are numbered 1, 3, 5, etc.
Each drawing is repeated twice in the Xsheet column
Drawings are numbered in reverse order
evidence_quote: an Increment: value 2 numbers the drawings 1, 3, 5, etc.

question: You want scanned drawings to be saved in a specific custom folder instead of the default location. Which approach achieves this?
options: Use the Path: field in the New Level dialog or in the Level Settings window to set the saving location
Set the Step: value to 2 so drawings are saved in the custom folder
Choose Scan Level from the Type: option menu to redirect the saving location
Double-click a cell and type a name and a number separated by a space
evidence_quote: You can change the location by using either the Path: field in the New Level dialog, or the Level Settings window in case you define a level directly in Xsheet/Timeline.

question: What does the "Save Default Settings" command do?
options: It saves the current scene file with all its settings under a new name
It makes the current scene's settings become the default values for all new scenes in that project
It exports the scene settings to a separate file that can be shared between projects
It resets all scene settings back to the project's original defaults
evidence_quote: all the settings from the current scene will become the project default

question: When you save a scene in OpenToonz, what happens to any changes you made to that scene's settings?
options: They are discarded unless you also save them as project defaults
They are automatically saved together with the scene
They are saved only if the settings dialog is still open
They are applied to all other scenes in the project
evidence_quote: Settings for a particular scene can always be changed independently from the other ones, and will be automatically saved when the scene is saved.

question: You are starting a production and want every new scene in your project to automatically use the same frame rate, camera size, and output options you just configured in your current scene. What should you do?
options: Use File → Project Management → Save Default Settings so the current scene's settings become the project default
Copy the scene file and use it as a template for each new scene
Manually open each settings dialog in every new scene and re-enter the values
Export the scene settings to a file and import it whenever you create a new scene
evidence_quote: If you want to change the default values you can save current scene settings as default, so that all new scenes created for that project will have those values.

question: In OpenToonz, where is the Key button used to set a palette color animation key located?
options: In the top bar of the Palette Editor
In the Style Editor's color wheel section
In the Xsheet toolbar at the top of the Xsheet
In the Scene Cast panel next to the level name
evidence_quote: Click the Key button ( ) in the top bar of the Palette Editor.

question: What does the Previous Key and Next Key buttons in the Palette Editor do when animating a palette?
options: They reorder the palette colors by moving the selected color one position back or forward in the list
They let you navigate between the frames where palette keys are set, to check the color animation
They shift the entire palette animation earlier or later along the Xsheet/Timeline
They cycle through the previous and next colors applied to the current drawing stroke
evidence_quote: Use the Previous Key ( ) and Next Key buttons ( ) available at the side of the key button in the top bar of the palette editor.

question: When checking for a palette key at a specific frame, how does the Key button in the Palette Editor indicate that the colors have a key at the current frame?
options: The Key button turns blue
The Key button starts blinking
The Key button label changes to 'KEY SET'
The Key button becomes grayed out
evidence_quote: if the Key button ( ) in the top bar of the Palette Editor is blue, the colors have a key at the current frame.

question: You want to make a level's colors change over time, for example shifting from one color at frame 1 to another at frame 20. Which feature lets you do this in OpenToonz?
options: Palette animation, by setting palette keys in the Palette Editor at the frames where colors should change
Motion tweening, by applying an interpolation to the level column in the Xsheet
Onion skin, by enabling it so colors blend between the previous and next drawings
Style branching, by linking several styles so they update together automatically
evidence_quote: For Toonz Vector and Toonz Raster levels, colors in a palette can be animated and changed according to the frames of the Xsheet/Timeline.

question: Which menu contains the Collapse command used to create a Sub-Xsheet from selected columns?
options: Level menu
Xsheet menu
File menu
Schematic menu
evidence_quote: Sub-Xsheets are managed by the Xsheet menu commands, and by buttons in the Xsheet Toolbar.

question: What does the Resequence command do to a Sub-Xsheet level?
options: It resets the Sub-Xsheet to the original length and order of its contents
It creates an independent copy of the Sub-Xsheet that can be edited separately
It brings all of the Sub-Xsheet contents into the main Xsheet/Timeline
It saves the Sub-Xsheet content as a standard scene file
evidence_quote: If you want to reset the editing of a Sub-Xsheet level, you can Resequence it, by resetting it to the original length and order of its contents.

question: What happens to the length of a closed Sub-Xsheet level when you edit its content afterwards?
options: It stays the same, because it depends on the number of frames its content lasted when the Sub-Xsheet was created
It automatically grows to match the new duration of the edited content
It shrinks whenever any frames are removed or added inside the Sub-Xsheet
It doubles in length each time the content is edited
evidence_quote: The closed Sub-Xsheet level length depends on how many frames its content lasts at the time you create it, and it is not affected when you edit the Sub-Xsheet content.

question: You want to edit a Sub-Xsheet's contents while still seeing the rest of the scene in the viewer. Which feature should you use and why?
options: Edit in Place, because it displays the whole scene contents while you edit the Sub-Xsheet
Clone Sub-Xsheet, because it duplicates the Sub-Xsheet so you can see both versions at once
Explode Sub-Xsheet, because it brings all contents into the main Xsheet where everything is visible
Resequence, because it restores the original order so the whole scene is visible
evidence_quote: When working inside a Sub-Xsheet, by default only its own contents are displayed in the viewer. If you need to edit the Sub-Xsheet contents while looking at the whole scene contents, you can activate the Edit in Place mode.

question: Where can you set the Skeleton tool's Mode, Global Key, and Show Only Active Skeleton options?
options: In the tool options bar
In the Stage Schematic
In the Xsheet column headers
In the Timeline layer properties dialog
evidence_quote: In the tool options bar you can set the following: Mode sets the operation to perform with the tool.

question: What is the purpose of the Skeleton tool?
options: To define a model by setting hierarchical links between its different sections exposed in different Xsheet columns (or Timeline layers), and animate it
To paint and color the different sections of a character model
To create new Xsheet columns or Timeline layers for each section of a model
To export a character model with its skeleton to other animation software
evidence_quote: The Skeleton tool ( ) allows you to define a model by setting hierarchical links between its different sections exposed in different Xsheet columns (or Timeline layers), and animate it.

question: What happens when the Global Key option is activated and you rotate a model section while animating the skeleton?
options: A key is automatically defined for the position, scaling and shearing transformations as well
Only a rotation key is defined, and no other transformations are affected
All transformations of every column in the scene receive a key
The rotation is applied to the parent section instead of the selected one
evidence_quote: This means that if you rotate a model section, automatically a key will be defined for the position, scaling and shearing transformations as well.

question: You are working with a character that has a highly complex skeleton and find it hard to manage because too many pivot points and skeleton lines are displayed. Which Skeleton tool option should you activate to make this easier, and why?
options: Show Only Active Skeleton, because it displays only the pivot points and the skeleton from the current section up to the parent section
Global Key, because it reduces the number of keys shown for each transformation
Build Skeleton mode, because it hides all sections that are not yet linked
Inverse Kinematics mode, because it removes the pivot points from the display
evidence_quote: Show Only Active Skeleton when activated displays only the pivot points and the skeleton from the current section up to the parent section: in this way it will be easier to manage characters with skeletons of a higher complexity.

question: In the OpenToonz particle effect settings, where would you define external forces like gravity and wind that affect particle behavior?
options: The Birth Parameters page
The Environment page
The Style Editor
The Defining Control Images panel
evidence_quote: Particles behavior defined by their birth parameters can be affected by external events, such as gravity and wind, that can be defined in the Environment page.

question: What does the Friction parameter do in the OpenToonz particle Environment settings?
options: It adds a constant speed to the particles in the direction set by an angle
It simulates a force opposite to the particles' motion in order to slow them down or stop them
It randomly displaces particles horizontally and vertically
It defines the direction in which gravity accelerates the particles
evidence_quote: Simulates a force which has a direction opposite to the motion of the particles, in order to slow them down, or to stop them.

question: In the OpenToonz particle Environment settings, what happens to the gravity direction when you increase the Gravity Angle value above 0?
options: The direction turns clockwise from the default downward direction
The direction turns counterclockwise from the default downward direction
The direction turns counterclockwise from the default upward direction
The gravity acceleration decreases as the angle increases
evidence_quote: Defines the gravity direction. The value 0 is for a downward direction; higher values turn the direction clockwise.

question: You want particles in an OpenToonz scene to drift steadily to the right at a constant speed, with no acceleration, starting at a specific frame. Which Environment setting should you use, and why?
options: Gravity, because it accelerates particles in a direction set by an angle
Wind, because it adds a constant speed to the particles without acceleration
Scattering, because it shifts particles to the right when values are positive
Friction, because a negative value makes particles accelerate in the direction of their own motion
evidence_quote: Simulates a speed that is added to the particles speed. The speed is constant, this means that there is no acceleration in the motion of the particles.

question: How do you open the Level Settings dialog for a level shown in the Scene Cast?
options: Double-click the level name in the Scene Cast and choose Properties from the dialog that opens
Right-click the level in the Scene Cast and choose Level Settings… from the menu that opens
Select the level and choose Scene → Scene Settings… from the menu bar
Choose Level → Level Settings… from the menu bar while the Scene Cast is active
evidence_quote: Right-click a level in the Scene Cast and choose Level Settings… from the menu that opens.

question: What does the Subsampling setting in the Level Settings dialog do?
options: It reduces the file size of the level on disk by lowering its resolution permanently
It sets how many pixels are skipped when the level is displayed in the work area, to speed up visualization and playback
It controls how many frames of the level are exposed per cell in the Xsheet
It adjusts the level's alpha channel so it renders correctly in previews
evidence_quote: Subsampling sets the simplifying factor to be applied to animation levels, clips and images when displayed in the work area in order to have a faster visualization and playback

question: What happens to a level's appearance when you increase the Antialias Softness value used with the Add Antialiasing option?
options: The edges of the level's lines become progressively smoother as the value increases
The level's colors become more saturated as the value increases
The level's transparency increases, making it more see-through as the value increases
The level's pixel shape becomes more square as the value increases
evidence_quote: The antialiasing value has to be specified in the Antialias Softness field, which can range from 0 to 100.

question: You have a level whose horizontal and vertical DPI differ, so it appears stretched on screen. Which setting makes it display properly?
options: Use Camera DPI, because it applies the camera's DPI to the level automatically
Premultiply, because it corrects the alpha channel so the image is not distorted
Forced Squared Pixel, because it forces a level with different horizontal and vertical DPI to have squared pixel shape
White As Transparent, because it replaces the white background with transparency, removing the stretched look
evidence_quote: Forced Squared Pixel forces a level that has a different horizontal and vertical DPI, and therefore is displayed stretched, to have the pixel shape squared, and thus to be displayed properly.

question: In OpenToonz's particle effects settings, where would you configure attributes like speed, size, mass, and lifetime that are assigned to each particle when it is generated and retained throughout its life?
options: In the Animation parameters page
In the Birth Params page
In the Defining Control Images section
In the Size Increase settings
evidence_quote: Those attributes can be set in the Birth Params page.

question: What does the 'Linked to Scale' option do for particle speed in OpenToonz?
options: It links the particle's speed to the animation frame rate, so particles speed up when the scene plays faster
It assigns each particle a speed value based on its Size value, so the largest particles are the fastest
It connects the particle speed to the control image brightness, making particles faster where the image is brighter
It forces all particles to share a single speed value taken from the maximum speed setting
evidence_quote: Assigns to each particle a speed value, taken between the minimum and maximum speed, according to the Size value applied to the particle. This causes the largest particles to be the fastest, emphasizing a depth of field effect.

question: In the particle Speed Angle setting, what happens as you increase the angle value above 0?
options: The direction turns counterclockwise from upward
The direction turns clockwise starting from an upward direction
The particles slow down proportionally to the angle
The particles reverse direction once the angle exceeds 90
evidence_quote: The value 0 is for an upward direction; higher values turn the direction clockwise.

question: You want a particle trail that spans 10 frames of motion but shows only five particles, one every two frames. Which setting achieves this and how?
options: Set the Trail value to 10 and the Step to 2, so the trail is 10 frames long with a particle visible every two frames
Set the Trail value to 5 and the Step to 2, so only five particles are generated in total
Set the Lifetime value to 10 and the Step to 5, so each particle lives ten frames but is visible for two
Set the Trail value to 2 and the Step to 10, so the trail repeats every ten frames
evidence_quote: For example, if the trail value is 10 and the step is set to 2, the trail will be 10 frames long, but only five particles, one every two frames, will be visible.

question: What is the purpose of the objects/effects tree in the Function Editor?
options: It displays the interpolation of the current transformation segment
It lets you select which objects/effects and parameters are displayed as a spreadsheet or curves in the area on the left
It saves and loads transformation data as CURVE files
It opens the Graph Editor in a separate popup window
evidence_quote: Clicking these icons allows you to select which object/effect and which parameters have to be displayed as a spreadsheet or curves in the area on the left.

question: In the Function Editor, what happens when you click and drag a separator toward the window border?
options: The section is hidden
The section is resized larger
The Graph Editor opens in a separate popup window
The Spreadsheet switches to the Graph Editor view
evidence_quote: Click and drag a separator toward the window border to hide a section.

question: You want to export a parameter's animation data so it can be used in other software. Which action in the Function Editor achieves this, and why?
options: Right-click the parameter in the objects/effects tree and choose Save Curve, because it saves the data as a CURVE file
Right-click the parameter in the objects and effects tree and choose Export Data, because it saves the data as a DAT file usable in other software
Right-click the folder in the objects/effects tree and choose Show Animated Only, because it isolates animated parameters for export
Click the Function Editor Toggle button, because it exports the visible curves to other software
evidence_quote: Right-click the relevant parameter in the objects and effects tree, and choose Export Data from the menu that opens. Use the Browser to choose a name and location for the file to be saved: the data will be saved as a DAT file that can be used in other software supporting this type of information.

question: When working with a Sub-Xsheet in the Plastic tool, at what point are the visible columns of the Sub-Xsheet taken into account for Mesh creation?
options: When the Create Mesh button is pressed
When the Sub-Xsheet is first selected as a starting element
When hidden levels are set to visible after mesh creation
When the mesh is rendered in the final output
evidence_quote: all of the columns in the Sub-Xsheet visible when the Create Mesh button is pressed, are taken into count for the creation of the Mesh.

question: What happens to levels that are hidden at the time the Mesh is created but are later set to visible?
options: They are deformed by Mesh transformations but only shown in render inside the mesh boundaries
They are fully visible in render and deformed by Mesh transformations like the other levels
They are ignored by the Mesh and render normally without any deformation
They replace the original mesh and become the new starting element
evidence_quote: they will be deformed by Mesh transformations, but they will be shown in render only inside the mesh boundaries

question: How does the visibility of columns in a Sub-Xsheet at the time of pressing the Create Mesh button affect the rendered output of those columns?
options: Columns visible at creation time are fully shown in render, while columns made visible afterward are only shown inside the mesh boundaries
All columns are shown in render regardless of their visibility at creation time
Columns hidden at creation time are removed from render permanently, even if made visible later
Columns visible at creation time are only shown inside the mesh boundaries, while hidden ones are fully visible
evidence_quote: These levels will be visible in render and will be deformed by Mesh transformations.

question: In which menu can you find the Cleanup command to process selected drawings in the Xsheet/Timeline?
options: Level → Cleanup
Scan & Cleanup → Cleanup
File → Cleanup
Edit → Cleanup
evidence_quote: In the Xsheet/Timeline select the drawings you want to process. Choose Scan & Cleanup  →  Cleanup .

question: What is the purpose of the Keep Original Cleaned Up Drawings As Backup option?
options: It saves a copy of the original scanned drawings before cleanup begins
It automatically creates a backup copy of the cleaned up drawings so the original can be retrieved if mistakes are made during painting
It duplicates the TLV file in a separate project folder each time the scene is saved
It stores an extra palette file alongside every cleaned up animation level
evidence_quote: It is also possible to automatically create a backup copy of the cleaned up drawings that will be stored in a subfolder named nopaint inside the same location where the cleaned up drawings are saved. In this way it will be possible to retrieve the original drawing in case some mistakes (e.g. a deletion of a drawing section) are made during the painting process.

question: What happens to a cell's color in the Xsheet after its drawing has been cleaned up?
options: It changes from light blue to green
It changes from green to light blue
It changes from white to yellow
It changes from grey to orange
evidence_quote: When a drawing is cleaned up, its cell color turns from light blue to green , the color denoting Toonz raster levels (see Working with Xsheet Columns ).

question: You want to run the cleanup of drawings exposed in a scene in the background while you keep working on other things in OpenToonz. Which approach should you use?
options: Use the Cleanup dialog and choose Cleanup All so no further prompts interrupt you
Activate the Visible Only option so only visible columns are processed
Add the scene as a cleanup task in the Tasks pane and execute it in batch mode
Save the scene and use File → Preferences → Drawing to enable the backup option
evidence_quote: The cleanup of drawings exposed in a scene can be added to a task list and performed in batch mode in order to run it in the background while you perform other work on your computer.

question: How can a user access the context menu to customize Plastic information display in the Viewer?
options: By clicking the right mouse button on the Viewer while the Plastic tool is active
By left-clicking the Viewer while the Plastic tool is active
By selecting the Display option from the main menu bar
By double-clicking the Plastic tool icon in the Tool Bar
evidence_quote: Clicking the right mouse button on the Viewer while the Plastic tool is active brings up a context menu.

question: When the Show Rigidity option is enabled, how does the Viewer visually represent areas of rigidity?
options: Rigidity is shown as red areas, while flexibility is shown as green areas
Rigidity is shown as blue areas, while flexibility is shown as yellow areas
Rigidity is shown as wireframe lines, while flexibility is shown as solid shapes
Rigidity is shown as darker shading, while flexibility is shown as lighter shading

question: Which setting must be enabled to visualize the Stacking Order values of the vertices using grey shading?
options: Show SO
Show Mesh
Show Rigidity
Show Skeleton Onion Skin
evidence_quote: If Show SO is enabled a grey shading shows the Stacking Order values of the vertices, where lighter areas will be on top, and darker ones behind.

question: What is the result of clicking and dragging a strip keyframe found in the horizontal strip?
options: All the keyframes it refers to will move along.
It deletes the keyframes from all visible curves.
It only moves the keyframe of the currently selected curve.
It changes the interpolation speed of the adjacent segments.
evidence_quote: Click and drag the strip keyframe: all the keyframes it refers to will move along.

question: How does moving the markers visible on the sides of the strip keyframes affect the animation?
options: It automatically changes the Ease In / Ease Out or the Speed In / Speed Out values of all the segments they refer to.
It adds new keyframes to the visible curves.
It shifts the timing of the keyframes to adjacent frames.
It toggles the visibility of the function curves.
evidence_quote: The markers can be moved, automatically changing the Ease In / Ease Out or the Speed In / Speed Out values of all the segments they refer to.

question: You want to add a keyframe to all visible curves at a specific frame simultaneously. What action should you take?
options: Ctrl-click (PC) or Cmd-click (Mac) the frame ruler.
Right-click the graph area and select "Add Key".
Drag a marker from the toolbar onto the graph.
Double-click the line connecting the keyframes.
evidence_quote: Ctrl-click (PC) or Cmd-click (Mac) the frame ruler where you want to add the keyframe: a keyframe will be added to all the visible curves.

question: In which panel is the interpolation mode controlled to set the speed of movements?
options: The Xsheet
The Function Editor
The Render Farm
The Library

question: What is the primary purpose of the animatic phase in a paperless production workflow within OpenToonz?
options: To decompose characters into multiple levels for skeleton components
To import storyboard drawings, adjust timing, and set camera movements
To apply special effects such as blur, glow, and color corrections
To batch-render scenes using a series of computers connected on a network

question: Which feature should be used to batch-render OpenToonz scenes by utilizing multiple computers connected on the same network?

The OpenToonz render farm
The Sub-Xsheets
The Graphic Design phase
evidence_quote: The OpenToonz render farm allows you to batch-render OpenToonz scenes by using a series of computers connected on the same network using TCP/IP.

question: What is the stated purpose of the scripting code example labeled 'Outline vectorization'?
options: To use the OutlineVectorizer on a single image.
To create an animation by rotating frames in a level.
To define the input and output folders for script images.
To show the resulting level in a flipbook window.
evidence_quote: This brief script is an example of using the OutlineVectorizer on a single image.

question: In which panel must you enter the mathematical expression to link skeleton vertices in Plastic Animation?
options: Function Editor
Xsheet
Timeline
Camera Settings
evidence_quote: by setting in the Function Editor the following expression in the Angle parameter of Shoulder_left

question: What capability does linking skeleton vertices with mathematical expressions provide during Plastic Animation?
options: Automatic actions where moving one vertex affects another
Automatic coloring of skeleton layers based on movement
Rendering optimization for mesh columns in the Timeline
Exporting skeleton data to external mathematical software
evidence_quote: This allows to set some automatic actions of the skeleton, for example you can link the main vertices of the shoulders, so that moving just one shoulder automatically moves the other.

question: How does appending "*-1" to a vertex angle expression affect the linked vertex's movement?

It doubles the speed of the rotation relative to the source
It locks the vertex in place preventing any movement
It reverses the column number reference in the expression

question: Where in the OpenToonz interface can you specify the full path to the FARMROOT folder?

In the Farm room, within the Batch Servers pane
In the Render Settings dialog under the Output tab
In the Startup Options window when launching the application

question: What is the primary function of OpenToonz when used with the Toonz Farm?

It serves as the client program to submit tasks and monitor farm status
It automatically configures the network permissions for the FARMROOT folder
It generates the controller.txt and servers.txt files automatically

question: Which scanning mode should be selected to preserve different line colors, such as a black character outline and a red body shadow, without requiring intensive painting work later?

Black and white
Greyscale
Autoadjust

question: Where can you configure the user account rights for the Toonz Farm Controller Windows Service?
options: Control Panel → System → Advanced Settings → Environment Variables
OpenToonz → File → Preferences → Farm Settings
Command Prompt → tfarmcontroller → config → user
Control Panel → Administrative Tools → Services → Properties → Log On page

question: What is created by the installation program when you choose to install the Farm Controller component?
options: A scheduled task named Toonz Farm Scheduler
A desktop shortcut named Toonz Farm Launcher
A system driver named Toonz Farm Driver
A Windows Service named Toonz Farm Controller
evidence_quote: When you choose to install the Farm Controller component, the installation program will create for the controller program a Windows Service, named Toonz Farm Controller .

question: To ensure the Toonz Farm Controller can access the FARMROOT folder shared by a remote host, what configuration change is required for the service?

Install the Farm Server component on the controller node only
Set the FARMROOT folder path to a local drive letter instead of UNC format

question: What is the specific function of the style labeled Color_0 in the palette?

It sets the default background color for the scene.
It applies a automatic texture to all vector strokes.
It locks all other styles from being edited.

question: How does adjusting the Alpha slider affect the appearance of a color style?
options: The lower the value, the more transparent the color.
The higher the value, the more transparent the color.
The lower the value, the more saturated the color.
The higher the value, the darker the color becomes.
evidence_quote: You can also set the opacity with the Alpha slider: the lower the value, the more transparent the color.

question: Where is the command located to open the dialog where you can define the resolution, range, step and shrink of the preview frames?
options: Render → Preview Settings…
File → Preferences… → Preview
Render → Preview
Window → Preview Settings
evidence_quote: Tip To set the scene preview settings: Choose Render → Preview Settings… . Set the options you want to use for the preview.

question: What is the purpose of the "Shrink" setting within the Preview Settings dialog?
options: It sets the reduction value for the previewed sequence resolution.
It sets the step for the rendered sequence.
It controls the resample used when images are scaled.
It sets the color depth for rendered images.

question: What is the effect of choosing a higher balance option for "Resample Balance" during preview rendering?
options: It increases the time needed for rendering the output.
It decreases the memory required to perform the preview.
It reduces the resolution of the previewed frames.
It automatically stitches frames to create the final preview.

question: You want to store the result of the compositing up to a specific effect node in memory so it will be reused without recomputation. Which action should you take?
options: Right-click the node and choose Cache FX.
